content.title: Housing Development Plans Get Wrecked by Congress - Bloomberg
content.text: OpinionEditorial BoardMarch 31, 2026 at 5:00 AM CDTBy The Editorial BoardThe Editorial Board publishes the views of the editors across a range of national and global affairs.FacebookXLinkedInEmailLinkGiftExpandNot ready.Photographer: Jordan Vonderhaar/BloombergFacebookXLinkedInEmailLinkGiftGift this articleAdd us on GoogleContact us:Provide news feedback or report an errorSite feedback:Take our SurveyNew WindowFacebookXLinkedInEmailLinkGiftBookmarkSaveTranslateTakeaways by Bloomberg AISubscribeAmong the few things that Americans agree on these days is that housing is too expensive. With a shortfall of at least 3.7 million homes, the obvious solution is to build more. Regrettably, a once-promising effort in Congress intended to do just that now seems to be falling apart — a victim of populist politics gone awry.Over the past two decades, home values have risen faster than incomes in much of the US. Rents have also soared in many cities, contributing to widespread worries about the cost of living. The main culprits are restrictive local zoning and land-use rules, which curb construction and investment.
